summary: The camera AI rules editor could not edit a rule. `withRouting` — the one place every config-rewriting path goes through, so that a mode change cannot drop a rule's destinations, PTZ recall or relay — was written as `const withRouting = (config) => applyPTZRecall(withRouting(config), ruleRecall)`. A function whose body calls itself with the same argument recurses until the stack dies, and SEVEN call sites route through it: changing the detection mode, the target classes, the line geometry, the crowd count, the dwell duration and the LPR config all threw RangeError and left the editor doing nothing. Shipped in #193 (W3-5b). It now re-applies destinations, PTZ recall and relay, which is what its own comment says it is for and what the destinations path already did by hand. ALSO FIXED, in the same screen: a face rule was invisible to the editor. `face` was missing from detectionModes, and modeFromDetectionType falls back to 'presence' for anything it does not know — so a face rule opened as a Presence rule and SAVING IT REWROTE detectionType to 'presence', silently ending face recognition on that camera and leaving a rule that fires on every person and car instead. A mode the editor cannot name is a rule the editor destroys. Face is now a first-class mode with its own panel (match mode, watchlist, minimum match confidence), the class picker is hidden for it exactly as for LPR, and two Save guards that assumed every rule has target classes and a zone are relaxed for it — a face rule has neither, so Save was permanently disabled and the rule could be opened but never saved. The zone is left EMPTY rather than seeded with the default polygon: empty means the whole frame, and quietly shrinking a doorway rule's coverage to the middle 70% of the picture during an unrelated save is worse than having no zone at all. Verified on the wire: the mode list now offers Face recognition, switching an ordinary rule to Crowd and toggling its classes works with an empty console, and a face rule survives an editor round trip (POST 200, detectionType still 'face', zonePolygon still empty, the new matchMode persisted).
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no API or schema change. Existing rules are unaffected except that editing one now works. A face rule created before this (by the People screen) opens as a face rule instead of a presence rule; anyone who opened and saved one previously will find it was converted to 'presence' and should switch it back — the People page's camera switch recreates it correctly. Frontend only. Adds 12 dictionary keys (vi.mode_face, vi.face*) in en/ms/zh/ar for the new face panel.
